Explanation.description:
ECO-01: why this gadget is in the answer, in the vocabulary the query
was written in.

The point is that an agent can justify a choice — to itself, to a user,
or in a chain plan — WITHOUT re-deriving semantics from gadget text.
Re-derivation from text is what the whole classifier exists to prevent,
and it is where an agent silently gets `mov rdi, rax ; ret` wrong.

It repeats `reads`, `stack_delta` and `terminator`, which also appear at
the top level of the record, deliberately: the object is meant to be
quotable on its own.

clobbers.description:
CLS-09 `clobbers`: registers written with a value the payload does
NOT decide. A clobber is not "unusable" — `mov rdi, rax ; ret`
clobbers rdi and tells you to control rax instead — but it is what
`no_clobber` rejects.

reads.description:
Registers read (`regs_read`): the inputs that must already hold what
you want.

sets.description:
CLS-09 `sets`: registers this gadget writes with a value the chain
PAYLOAD decides. This is what `set_reg` matches, and it is a strict
subset of `regs_written` — `xor rdi, rdi ; ret` writes rdi and sets
nothing.

stack_delta.description:
Net stack-pointer movement in bytes, terminator included. `null`
means UNKNOWN (a non-constant effect, an unmodelled form, or the
text classification path) and must never be read as zero.

terminator.description:
CLS-09 terminator class: `ret`, `ret-imm`, `jmp-reg`, `jmp-mem`,
`call-reg`, `call-mem`, `syscall`, `far`, `other`. Finer than the
record's `terminator`, and the spelling the `terminator` filter
accepts.

why.description:
One sentence naming the payload offset each set register comes from,
what is clobbered, the stack movement and the terminator.

description: Find gadgets by their EFFECT, not their text: "set rdi from the stack, preserve rsi and rdx, at most one side effect, a clean ret" is one call. own pop included — `pop rdi ; ret` is 16 on x86-64. CLS-09 landed
the computation in v0.4; the field existed (always `null`) in v0.3
so the record shape would not change when it did.

`null` is UNKNOWN, not zero: a non-constant effect (`xchg rsp,
rax`), an architecture or instruction form the model does not prove,
or a gadget classified from text. `max_stack_delta` rejects it
rather than assuming.

terminator.description:
How the gadget hands control on: `ret`, `ret-imm`, `retf`, `iret`,
`far`, `jmp`, `call`, `syscall`, `none`.

vaddr.description:
Zero-padded hex address, for humans. The padding width is 8 on a
32-bit target and 16 on a 64-bit one, which is why `vaddr_u64`
exists.

vaddr_u64.description:
The same address as a number. Agents doing arithmetic should use
this and never parse `vaddr`.

Warning.description:
A non-fatal fact the agent has to know to read the result correctly
(CRIT-03 item 4).

`fallback_section_names` used to be a bare boolean with no explanation,
and truncation was announced nowhere at all. Every entry has a stable
`code` to branch on and a `message` to show a human.

detail.description: Free-form detail (the slice name, the architecture, …).

field.description: The response field the warning is about, when it is about one.

binary_label.description:
The binary's path relative to its allow root — what the audit log
records, and never the caller's spelling of the path.

cache.description:
`hit` when the gadget set came from a cache (in memory, pinned for

cache_key.description: Key of the cached scan; the second path component of `resource_uri`.

fallback_section_names.description:
The binary has no section names and synthetic `PT_LOAD#n` names were
matched instead. Also reported in `warnings`.

next_cursor.description:
Opaque token for the next page; `null` on the last one. Send it back
as `cursor` with the SAME query parameters.

offset.description: Index of this page's first gadget within the ordered result.

order.description:
The order actually applied: `rank`, `address`, `quality`, `text` or
`ids`. Echoed because the default changed to `rank` and an agent
must not have to assume.

resource_uri.description:
`ropfinder://scan/<cache_key>/gadgets.ndjson` — the WHOLE ordered
result, one `GadgetRecord` per line, readable with `resources/read`.
Present only when the result was paged.

total_count.description: Gadgets matching the query, before paging.

warnings.description: Non-fatal facts. Always present; `[]` when there are none.

workspace_file.description:
The same NDJSON as a real file, when the server was started with
`--workspace-dir`. An agent with filesystem tools should grep this
instead of paging.

description: Search gadgets by pattern: regex matched against gadget text (e.g. "pop r.*; ret"); invalid regexes fall back to literal substring match. Runs a full ROP+JOP+SYS scan, then filters. Same ranking, semantic filters, cursor and caps as find_gadgets.

arch.description:
Architecture slice for a fat (Universal) Mach-O, e.g. "x86_64",
"arm64", "i386". REQUIRED for a multi-slice container: without it
the scan is refused rather than concatenating slices whose virtual
address ranges overlap (CORE-03).

badbytes.description: Reject gadgets whose final address contains these bytes.

base.description: Rebase the image base at load time (hex string).

binary_path.description:
Absolute path to the binary; must be inside one of the server's
allow_roots (get_server_config lists them).

class.description: Keep only gadgets whose primary class is one of these.

cursor.description: `next_cursor` from a previous page of THIS query.

from_stack.description: Require the `writes_reg` registers to come off the stack.

label.description: Keep only gadgets carrying at least one of these labels.

max_results.description: Maximum gadgets returned per page (default 1000, hard max 50000).

max_stack_delta.description:
ECO-01: keep only gadgets whose net stack movement is KNOWN and at
most this many bytes (the terminator's own pop included, so
`pop rdi ; ret` is 16 on x86-64). A gadget whose delta is unknown is
REJECTED, never assumed to be 0.

no_clobber.description:
ECO-01: none of these registers may be CLOBBERED — written with a
value the payload does not decide. Matched against the classifier's
`clobbers`, NOT `regs_written`: `pop rdi ; ret` survives
`no_clobber: ["rdi"]` and `mov rdi, rax ; ret` does not. Elements
may also be comma-separated.

offset.description: Offset added to gadget addresses (hex string).

pattern.description:
Regex matched against gadget text (e.g. "pop r.*; ret"); if the
pattern is not a valid regex it is matched as a literal substring.

pivot.description:
ECO-12: the stack-pivot preset — keep only gadgets carrying the
`stack-pivot` label.

preserves_regs.description: Keep only gadgets that write NONE of these registers.

reads_reg.description: Keep only gadgets that read ALL of these registers.

search.description:
ECO-01: ropper-style wildcard matcher over the instruction
SEQUENCE, e.g. "pop rdi; ret". `?` is one character, `%` is any run
inside one instruction (so a bare `%` is any single instruction).
The instructions must appear as a contiguous run, so
"pop rdi; ret" also matches "xor eax, eax ; pop rdi ; ret".

set_reg.description:
ECO-01: keep only gadgets that SET all of these registers — write
them with a value the chain PAYLOAD decides. Strictly stronger than
`writes_reg`: `xor rdi, rdi ; ret` writes rdi and sets nothing.

terminator.description:
Terminator kind: "ret", "jmp", "call", "syscall", "none", "any",
or a CLS-09 class ("bare-ret", "ret-imm", "jmp-reg", "jmp-mem",
"call-reg", "call-mem", "far", "other").

writes_reg.description: Keep only gadgets that write ALL of these registers.

name: search_gadgets_by_pattern

Explanation.description:
ECO-01: why this gadget is in the answer, in the vocabulary the query
was written in.

The point is that an agent can justify a choice — to itself, to a user,
or in a chain plan — WITHOUT re-deriving semantics from gadget text.
Re-derivation from text is what the whole classifier exists to prevent,
and it is where an agent silently gets `mov rdi, rax ; ret` wrong.

It repeats `reads`, `stack_delta` and `terminator`, which also appear at
the top level of the record, deliberately: the object is meant to be
quotable on its own.

clobbers.description:
CLS-09 `clobbers`: registers written with a value the payload does
NOT decide. A clobber is not "unusable" — `mov rdi, rax ; ret`
clobbers rdi and tells you to control rax instead — but it is what
`no_clobber` rejects.

reads.description:
Registers read (`regs_read`): the inputs that must already hold what
you want.

sets.description:
CLS-09 `sets`: registers this gadget writes with a value the chain
PAYLOAD decides. This is what `set_reg` matches, and it is a strict
subset of `regs_written` — `xor rdi, rdi ; ret` writes rdi and sets
nothing.

stack_delta.description:
Net stack-pointer movement in bytes, terminator included. `null`
means UNKNOWN (a non-constant effect, an unmodelled form, or the
text classification path) and must never be read as zero.

terminator.description:
CLS-09 terminator class: `ret`, `ret-imm`, `jmp-reg`, `jmp-mem`,
`call-reg`, `call-mem`, `syscall`, `far`, `other`. Finer than the
record's `terminator`, and the spelling the `terminator` filter
accepts.

why.description:
One sentence naming the payload offset each set register comes from,
what is clobbered, the stack movement and the terminator.

GadgetRecord.description:
One gadget, in the shape every gadget-returning tool emits.

Invariant: the field set does not depend on the request. A gadget from a
scan with no `section` parameter carries `"section": null`, not a missing
key; an x86-64 ELF carries `"arch": null` and `"delay_slot": false`, not
nothing at all. `tests/schema_conformance.rs` asserts the four shapes
that used to differ — plain, `section=.text`, MIPS, and the fat Mach-O —
have identical key sets.

arch.description:
Fat Mach-O slice this gadget came from; `null` for every other
container.

class.description:
Primary class (`reg-write`, `stack-pivot`, `mem-read`, `mem-write`,
`arithmetic`, `syscall`, `dispatcher`, `other`); `null` when the
architecture has no classifier.

delay_slot.description:
MIPS/SPARC: the LAST instruction is the branch's delay slot, so it
executes **before** control transfers. `rf_scan` has always computed
this and every output boundary dropped it.

explanation.description: ECO-01: why this gadget is here, in the query's own vocabulary.

id.description:
Stable identity: `g_` + base32 of the first 10 bytes of
`blake3(binary_sha256 || vaddr_le || bytes)`. Independent of every
scan parameter, so the same gadget has the same id across calls,
processes and cache evictions. Pass a list of these to
`get_gadgets`.

labels.description: Every class the gadget earns, not just the primary one.

low_confidence.description:
The classification came from disassembly text rather than decoder
metadata, so treat the semantic fields as advisory.

privileged.description:
Contains a privileged or undefined instruction, so it faults in user
mode and cannot appear in a chain.

quality.description: TAXONOMY.md R12 quality score, higher is cleaner.

regs_from_stack.description:
The subset of `regs_written` loaded off the stack — the registers a
chain payload can actually control.

regs_written.description: Registers the gadget writes, lowercase and sigil-free.

section.description:
Section containing the gadget; `null` when no `section` filter was
applied (the scan then has no section table to consult).

side_effects.description: Instructions that earn at least one label.
